- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a recent price spike, model often overshoots downward in the next few days; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged sell-off momentum.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates the continuation; add a small upward adjustment to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon; apply a small upward bias to the early period to account for mean reversion toward recent highs.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/– 0.3), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast transitions and avoid sharp directional shifts.
